relevance_reason: Reports a new SERPINH1 (HSP47) mutation causing recessive OI and studies how it affects HSP47 and FKBP65 in cells. SERPINH1 is the gene for OI type X.

findings.statement: Duran et al. (2015) identified a new osteogenesis imperfecta mutation in the SERPINH1 gene. The mutation destabilized HSP47 and caused it to be mislocalized, and it secondarily had similar effects on FKBP65.
quotes: We have identified a new OI mutation in SERPINH1 that results in destabilization and mislocalization of HSP47 and secondarily has similar effects on FKBP65.

findings.statement: Duran et al. (2015) found evidence that HSP47 and FKBP65 act cooperatively during posttranslational maturation of type I procollagen, and that the two proteins fail to interact properly in cells with mutant HSP47. They concluded that OI caused by HSP47 deficiency and OI caused by FKBP65 deficiency share a common cellular pathway.
quotes: We found evidence that HSP47 and FKBP65 act cooperatively during posttranslational maturation of type I procollagen and that FKBP65 and HSP47 but fail to properly interact in mutant HSP47 cells.
These results thus reveal a common cellular pathway in cases of OI caused by HSP47 and FKBP65 deficiency.

relevance_reason: The paper reports the SERPINH1 homozygous missense mutation that causes severe recessive OI (OI type X), together with functional studies.

findings.statement: In an individual with severe autosomal recessive osteogenesis imperfecta, Christiansen et al. (2010) identified a homozygous missense mutation (c.233T>C, p.Leu78Pro) in the SERPINH1 gene, which encodes the collagen chaperone-like protein HSP47.
quotes: We have identified an autosomal-recessive missense mutation (c.233T>C, p.Leu78Pro) in SERPINH1, which encodes the collagen chaperone-like protein HSP47, that leads to a severe OI phenotype.

findings.statement: Christiansen et al. (2010) found that the L78P mutation caused the endoplasmic reticulum-resident HSP47 to be degraded via the proteasome. In fibroblasts from the affected individual, type I procollagen accumulated in the Golgi, and part of the secreted type I procollagen was protease sensitive. The authors suggested that HSP47 monitors the integrity of the type I procollagen triple helix at the ER/cis-Golgi boundary, and that without it procollagen moves from the ER to the Golgi faster and its helical structure is compromised.
quotes: The mutation results in degradation of the endoplasmic reticulum resident HSP47 via the proteasome.
Type I procollagen accumulates in the Golgi of fibroblasts from the affected individual and a population of the secreted type I procollagen is protease sensitive.

These findings suggest that HSP47 monitors the integrity of the triple helix of type I procollagen at the ER/cis-Golgi boundary and, when absent, the rate of transit from the ER to the Golgi is increased and helical structure is compromised.

findings.statement: Christiansen et al. (2010) found normal 3-hydroxylation of the prolyl residue at position 986 of the proalpha1(I) triple helical domain in the patient. They concluded that HSP47 acts downstream of the CRTAP/P3H1/CyPB complex involved in prolyl 3-hydroxylation.
quotes: The normal 3-hydroxylation of the prolyl residue at position 986 of the triple helical domain of proalpha1(I) chains places the role of HSP47 downstream from the CRTAP/P3H1/CyPB complex that is involved in prolyl 3-hydroxylation.
